title: Make Sum Divisible by P
statement:
You are given an array of positive integers `nums` and an integer `p`. You may delete one contiguous block of elements (possibly an empty block, but never the entire array) so that the sum of the elements that remain is a multiple of `p`.

Return the minimum length of such a block, or `-1` when no allowed deletion makes the remaining sum divisible by `p`.
notes:
## Intuition

Let the whole sum leave remainder `need` when divided by `p`. Deleting a block fixes the sum exactly when the block's own sum also leaves remainder `need`. A block `nums[j + 1 .. i]` sums to `prefix(i) - prefix(j)`, so we want an earlier prefix whose remainder equals `(prefix(i) - need) mod p`. Trying every block is O(n²); remembering the latest index of each prefix remainder in a map answers this in O(1) per step.

## Approach

1. Compute `need`, the total sum modulo `p`. If it is `0`, nothing has to go: return `0`.
2. Store remainder `0` at index `-1` in `lastIndex` (the empty prefix).
3. Walk through `nums`, keeping `prefix` as the running sum modulo `p`.
4. The block ending at `i` works if some earlier prefix had remainder `wanted = (prefix - need + p) % p`; its length is `i - lastIndex.get(wanted)`. Keep the smallest in `shortest`.
5. Save `i` as the latest index for `prefix`; later blocks want the latest start because it is the shortest.
6. A best length equal to `nums.length` means only the whole array works, which is forbidden: return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 1, 4, 2]`, `p = 6`. The sum is `10`, so `need = 4`.

- `i = 0`: `prefix = 3`, `wanted = 5` is unseen. Save `3 → 0`.
- `i = 1`: `prefix = 4`, `wanted = 0` is at `-1`, length `2`. Save `4 → 1`.
- `i = 2`: `prefix = 2`, `wanted = 4` is at `1`, length `1` (the block `[4]`).
- `i = 3`: `prefix = 4`, `wanted = 0` gives length `4`, no better.

The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for the total and one pass with constant-time map work.
- Space: O(min(n, p)) for the remainders stored in `lastIndex`.

## Pitfalls

- Reduce modulo `p` at every step; raw sums can reach 10^14, which overflows 32-bit integers in Java or C.
- Add `p` before taking `% p` in `wanted`, because `prefix - need` may be negative.
- Removing the whole array is not allowed, so a best length of `nums.length` must become `-1`.
- Overwrite the stored index for a remainder each time; keeping the first index would give longer blocks.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `need` | total sum modulo `p`; the remainder the removed block must have |
| `lastIndex` | map from a prefix remainder to the latest index where it occurred |
| `prefix` | sum of `nums[0..i]` modulo `p` |
| `wanted` | the earlier prefix remainder that makes the block end at `i` work |
| `shortest` | smallest valid block length so far (`nums.length` means none yet) |
